sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: This species is difficult to identify morphologically because it is intermediate between I. finitimus and I. phalloides; identification is clearly easier from COII sequences, this species forming a clade distinctly separate from the finitimus clade. Without molecular data the best approach combines the worker enteric valve architecture (EVA), the degree of soldier mandibular curvature and the geographic origin. The worker EVA is of the finitimus type; the workers are medium-sized within the genus but the enteric valve is rather small. The soldier left mandible apical curvature index averages, together with that of I. fungifaber, the highest in the genus; body size medium within the genus; the setae on the odd primary cushion of its enteric valve become very dense, indicating the position of the crest in the worker valve, so that the finitimus architecture is recognisable. The alate is medium-sized within the genus, the compound eyes and ocelli averaging larger than in I. finitimus. The species is also defined by ecology and distribution: it always occurs in evergreen forest from Gabon to the Central African Republic, at most about 1000 km from the Atlantic coast. Some specimens resemble I. fungifaber but differ in EVA; some resemble I. phalloides with a similar EVA but differ in caecum and distribution; most resemble I. finitimus with similar EVA and caecum but differ in distribution, the two overlapping in the Central African Republic.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule well sclerotized, very dark in fresh specimens (C7–C8), C6–C7 in long-preserved material; frontal gland pore concolorous with the head capsule or slightly paler; postclypeus C6–C7, one shade paler than the head capsule; antennae C5–C6, without difference between proximal and apical segments. Pronotum C6–C7, concolorous with the postclypeus, generally one shade paler than the head capsule; meso- and metanotum C5–C6, concolorous with the pronotum or slightly paler; legs C3–C5, the tibiae usually one shade darker than the femora; wings transparent with a brown to grey tinge (Cf3–Cf4), the costa darker; abdominal tergites C6–C7; sternites distinctly paler in the middle (C2–C5), darker at the sides (C4–C6), the posterior sternites (C4–C6) darker than the anterior ones. Head capsule with conspicuous setae scattered among the dense felt of short fine hairs; labrum and postclypeus with conspicuous setae mixed with short hairs; antennae with conspicuous setae and more numerous small hairs, most segments with a tuft of very fine curved hairs at the tip, especially distally (visible above 50×). Pronotum setae mainly on the margins, shorter in the middle; meso- and metanotum with fine pale hairs arranged along the median band (generally visible at 20–40×). Legs hairy, the fore coxa with 6–10 stronger setae on the ridge and 1–4 ventrally, sometimes also on the trochanter; fore, mid and hind tibiae with 3, 2 and 2 apical spurs and 0, 2 and 0 subapical spurs respectively, the tibiae with 15–30 spines. Abdominal tergites with setae of mixed sizes; sternites with long setae erect or slightly inclined forward, together with many long and small setae directed posteriorly. Compound eyes nearly circular; ocelli nearly circular to oval, separated from the compound eye by about 0.7–1.2 times the small ocellar diameter; frontal gland pore generally a small circular mark. Antennae 16-segmented in alates, the queen and male always with fewer segments through breakage. Labrum domed. Left mandible apical tooth on average smaller than in most species of the genus, but always more prominent than the first marginal tooth; 3 marginal teeth, the second expressed only as an undulation of the tooth margin between the first and third; only the apical tooth sharp in unworn specimens; the proximal premolar hidden or partly hidden by the molar prominence in dorsal view; the dorsal surface of the molar with a rounded prominence ending posteriorly in a small sharp process. Right mandible apical tooth always more prominent than the first marginal tooth; 2 marginal teeth, the first sharp-tipped when fresh, the second smaller and blunt even when fresh; the molar with a rounded labial process ventrally and heel-shaped posteriorly. Pronotum distinctly wider than long, narrower than the head width (including compound eyes), flat to very weakly saddle-shaped, the anterior lobe short and very slightly raised; the fore coxa with a lip-like projection ventrally forming a more or less sharp ridge. Wings: R1 completely fused with the margin and sclerotized; Rs single and sclerotized; M and Cu unsclerotized or weakly sclerotized, with 3–4 and 10–11 branches respectively. Gut not studied (enteric valve not studied). Measurements: compound eye major diameter 0.41–0.47 mm, head width including compound eyes 1.49–1.67 mm, distance from the apical tooth to the first marginal tooth 0.19–0.23 mm, ocellus major diameter 0.15–0.19 mm, postclypeus width 0.72–0.81 mm, pronotum width 1.36–1.57 mm, hind tibia length 1.30–2.00 mm, fore wing length to the suture 13.6–14.0 mm (n = 4).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule on the dark side (Cd4–Cd5), paler in long-preserved specimens; always grading from a darker frons to a paler posterior (e.g. C5→C4), smooth and extended in 60% of the specimens examined, more abrupt in the remaining 40%, so that the head capsule may look bicoloured; antennae and labrum sometimes concolorous with the head capsule or one shade paler; mandibles dark (C6–C8), the base generally abruptly two shades paler and generally concolorous with the frons; thorax and legs paler than the head capsule (C2–C4), slightly darker in long-preserved specimens; abdomen grey to red-brown from the gut contents. Head capsule with a few scattered setae; a dense tuft of hairs surrounds and covers the frontal gland pore; antennae with conspicuous setae and more numerous small hairs, the apical segment with a tuft of very fine curved hairs at its tip (visible above 50×); the labrum always with several large setae on each lobe; pronotum and mesonotum with few setae, mainly on the margins. Fore coxa with at least 1 fine seta, without spines in 10% of the specimens examined, generally with 1–4 spines on the ridge and none ventrally; trochanter generally with rows of long setae, sometimes with 5–6 spines; fore, mid and hind tibiae with 3, 2 and 2 apical spurs and 0, 2 and 0 subapical spurs respectively (the latter sometimes weak), each tibia with a row of 6–15 spines. Abdominal tergites with the large setae mainly or only on the posterior margin; sternites with long setae erect or slightly inclined forward and often pigmented, together with smaller setae directed posteriorly. Soldier medium-sized within the genus. Head capsule distinctly sclerotized, distinctly longer than wide; in dorsal view the sides nearly parallel, narrowing in the posterior 1/3–1/4, converging from the antennal sockets more or less towards the mandible bases, the posterior margin regularly rounded, briefly straight in the middle in 56% of the specimens examined; the upper margin almost always slightly concave; the angle between the projecting mandibles and the frons always slightly obtuse; frons generally (88%) without an anterior swelling, rarely with a weak one. Gulamentum narrowing in the posterior half in ventral view, the anterior half either rounded at the sides or widening at sharp angles, and even (36% of the specimens examined) ear-like. Antennae 15-segmented. Labrum always deeply forked, wider than long, the sides from harp-shaped (92% of the specimens examined) to straight; the lobes angular, their tips often fine, white or semitransparent; the anterior margin concave. Mandibles sabre-like, strongly curved (on average the left mandible apical curvature index of I. fungifaber and I. planifrons is the highest in the genus); the inner margin generally smooth, each mandible with 1 distinct but generally very small marginal tooth near the molar area; mandibles distinctly shorter than the head; the surface of both smooth and shining; the right mandible generally slightly more curved than the left. Pronotum saddle-shaped, 56%–64% of the head width, the anterior and posterior margins generally entire; the fore coxa with a lip-like projection ventrally forming a more or less sharp ridge. Enteric valve inserted on the left side, best seen in ventral view, in the posterior half of the abdomen. Primary cushions (PC) arranged with trigonal symmetry, the odd cushion about 20% longer than the even ones, generally without a crest or with a very weak one. Caecum always small, best seen in ventral view, near the middle of the abdomen, with short lobes. Measurements: head dorsal concavity sagitta 0.00–0.06 mm, head length 2.60–3.45 mm, head width 1.83–2.34 mm, left mandible ventral length 2.13–2.62 mm, left mandible minor curvature 0.19–0.35 mm, hind tibia length 1.50–1.89 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule pale (C1–C3), turning grey in long-preserved specimens; proximal antennal segments pale (C2–C3), the apical segment always 1–2 shades darker (C4–C5); thorax, tergites and legs pale (C1–C3); abdomen grey to red-brown from the gut contents. Head capsule and postclypeus with a few scattered erect setae; labrum with a few scattered stout setae; antennae with conspicuous setae and more numerous small hairs, the apical segment with a tuft of fine curved hairs at its tip (visible above 50×); thoracic tergites with scattered setae. Fore coxa ridged, with 1 fine seta, 3–5 spines on the ridge and generally 1 ventrally (very rarely 2–3); fore trochanter with 5–7 spines; fore, mid and hind tibiae with 3, 2 and 2 apical spurs and 0, 2 and 0 subapical spurs respectively (the latter sometimes weak), and with a row of spines. Abdominal tergites with scattered setae; sternites with long setae erect or slightly inclined forward and often pigmented, together with smaller setae directed posteriorly. Workers medium-sized on average within the genus, with much overlap with several species. Head capsule weakly sclerotized (except the mandibles). Antennae 14.5 segmented. Labrum domed. Left mandible with a well-developed apical tooth, sharp-tipped when fresh; 3 marginal teeth, the first well developed but blunt even when fresh, the second weak (expressed only as an undulating tooth margin, lost with wear), the third with a blunt tip; the proximal premolar generally hidden by the molar prominence; the dorsal surface of the molar with a rounded prominence ending posteriorly in a small sharp process. Right mandible with a well-developed apical tooth, sharp when fresh; 2 marginal teeth, the first well developed and sharp when fresh, the second smaller and blunt even when fresh; the molar with a rounded labial process ventrally and heel-shaped posteriorly. Pronotum saddle-shaped, 63%–76% of the head width; the fore coxa with a lip-like projection ventrally forming a sharp ridge. Enteric valve inserted on the left, best seen in ventral view, in the posterior half of the abdomen. Primary cushions arranged in the finitimus type with trigonal symmetry: the downstream part of the odd cushion is broad, its bulbous inflation bearing denser shorter setae; supporting setae generally numerous, 17–31 on each side of the odd cushion; secondary cushions broad upstream, distinctly narrowing downstream, the spines evenly distributed. Caecum always small, visible in ventral view, near the middle of the abdomen, with short lobes (generally 3 lobules). Measurements: maximum head width 1.08–1.30 mm, distance from the left apical tooth to the first marginal tooth 0.16–0.20 mm, left mandible functional length 0.55–0.64 mm, hind tibia length 1.18–1.48 mm, mean length of primary cushions 1–6 0.49–0.66 mm, mean width 0.05–0.10 mm, mean length of secondary cushions 0.38–0.51 mm, mean width 0.18–0.27 mm, odd primary cushion elongation index WVPOdd-Elg = 5.48–9.57.

note: Adapted from the genus revision in Josens et al. (2025), original in English; the alate enteric valve was not studied in the original (enteric valve not studied); measurements from Table 12 and the text of the original; distribution, hosts, DNA and figure numbers are not translated.
